event: William Blair 44th Annual Growth Stock Conference
rows: William Blair 44th Annual Growth Stock Conference
Canada, UK, Ireland, Australia, France, New Zealand
Slide-driven presentation positioning Celsius as the disruptor of the Red Bull / Monster energy-drink duopoly - the #3 US energy brand and first in a decade to exceed 10% share.
20-year evolution narrative: from a 'negative calorie' beverage near insolvency in 2011 to a fitness-rooted, science-backed 'live fit' brand.
Structural tailwind: total beverage declining while energy grows; retailers shifting shelf space to energy from CSDs, water, dairy, coffee - Celsius the biggest beneficiary.
Unique incrementality: 41% of growth is new-to-category and 79% of consumption is new-to-category, so Celsius's retail dollar 'travels further' than other brands.

Acknowledged headwind: Pepsi inventory 'noise' - the pullback was in days-on-hand, not total cases; attributed to Pepsi getting more efficient in its second full year. Conceded it 'creates noise for us as a publicly traded company.'
2024 framed as the biggest growth year ever; at 98% ACV, focus is breadth/depth within the store rather than store count.
Refused to quantify shelf-space gains - deferred to end-of-month Circana SKU-per-location data; cited Maverik example (three facings in December to ~a shelf and a half in 2024).
Resets need time to 'marinate' before consumers show up - tempering near-term expectations; Circle K and some Kroger divisions still had resets to complete.
Methodical five-year international plan: Canada at 5.5% share, UK/Ireland launched, Australia/France/New Zealand planned for Q4 2024; disciplined - 'not looking to just blow cash.'
Clear long-term ambition to close the ~$3 billion gap to Monster's US business via new-to-category compounding.

Portfolio: bifurcated core/Vibe lines (same formula, 24 flavors, 'billboard effect'), the new Essentials 16-oz can (Q4 2023 launch at 7-Eleven, ~50% of category is 16-oz), and On The Go powder sticks.
F1/Ferrari partnership positioned as a brand-building catalyst across Europe, APAC and the US; sugar-free category at an inflection point ('getting ready to flip for the first time').
Asked for an update on shelf-space gains and how far along Celsius is in the reset process.

Said retailers are giving Celsius more space and it is the biggest beneficiary; Celsius has not publicly stated where it will land but said 2024 will be its biggest growth year ever. At 98% ACV, growth is about breadth/depth within the store. Cited Maverik - moving from three facings in a 'three-door set' in December to ~a shelf and a half in 2024 - and said end-of-month Circana data will show SKUs per location. Resets remained at Circle K and some Kroger divisions; reset locations need time to 'marinate' before velocity builds.
Asked about leveraging major events such as the Olympics for marketing (question inaudible in transcript).

Said the timing makes the Olympics tough to leverage given the Q4 launch cadence; Celsius has discussed grassroots events but nothing major. Pointed to the recent Monaco F1 race and the Ferrari partnership - taking retailers to events builds goodwill - and said the F1/Ferrari deal will be excellent for Europe, APAC and the US; any Olympics involvement would not be significant.
Asked about production capacity and the ability to scale (question inaudible in transcript).

Said Chief Supply Chain Officer Paul Storey came from Monster (head of global ops four years; also built Rockstar's footprint) with best-in-class relationships with the three major global can manufacturers. Celsius owns no production - it outsources everything, using over 20 US co-packers plus co-packing in Europe and Asia, with production planned in Australia at launch. Storey challenges the sales team weekly to outsell production capacity, giving confidence Celsius can scale.
Asked about the Pepsi inventory pullback (question inaudible in transcript).

Clarified the inventory pullback was in days-on-hand, not total cases - sales continue to grow, so Celsius tracks inventory as days-on-hand. Attributed it to Pepsi getting more efficient in its second full year, understanding Celsius's SKU portfolio, and determining the appropriate inventory level - like any good business drawing down raw-material inventory. As long as accounts are serviced there are no complaints, though it 'creates noise' for a publicly traded company; management had no updates beyond prior public statements.
